summary: Ngo Dac proves the algebraic half of the Todd–Thakur analogues of the Zagier–Hoffman conjectures for multiple zeta values over F_q[θ]: for every weight w, the Thakur family T_w spans the weight-w MZVs over K (Theorem A, by an algorithm built on Thakur's power-sum products and Todd's operations B* and C). On the transcendental side, the MZVs with all entries below q are linearly independent (Theorem B, through the Anderson–Brownawell–Papanikolas criterion applied to merged Anderson–Thakur t-motives). Together these give the Thakur basis theorem for w ≤ q (Corollary C) and, with the q-indivisible family, for w ≤ 2q − 2 (Theorem D). 108 items (5 library, 3 planned, 100 missing) are routed to DrinfeldModulesAndTModules (DM.0, DM.2, DM.4, DM.6, DM.8) and to the proposed DrinfeldModulesAndTModulesPartII. Twelve findings are recorded: eight in the manuscript (E1–E6, E11, E12), including an ABP criterion stated without c ≠ 0 and an integrality step in §6 that needs δ ∈ A[t], and four in cited sources (E7–E10).

items.name: Infinity valuation and valued completion
items.statement: For a field F, RatFunc F has multiplicative infinity valuation exp(intDegree), with zero sent to zero, and its uniform completion is a valued field. Specialize F=F_q; the paper's additive valuation on θ is −1.
items.locator: §1 notation; Mathlib/FieldTheory/RatFunc/Valuation.lean, declarations and statements read at pinned commit

api.name: CharPMZV.infinity.on_polynomials
api.statement: A nonzero polynomial has multiplicative value exp(natDegree).

api.name: CharPMZV.infinity.completion_map
api.statement: The canonical map to CompletionAtInfty preserves the valuation.

uses.how: Carrier of all MZV sums.

items.name: Positive indices, weight and depth
items.statement: An index is a finite list of positive integers, with weight its sum and depth its length; its i-th coordinate is zero for i past the length.

api.name: CharPMZV.indices.weight_append
api.statement: Weight of concatenation equals sum of weights.

api.name: CharPMZV.indices.depth_bound
api.statement: Depth is at most weight; weight zero iff the list is empty.

api.name: CharPMZV.indices.coordinate
api.statement: Inside its length an index coordinate is positive; outside it is zero.

uses.how: Parameters of every power sum and finite induction.

items.name: Prefix dominance on indices
items.statement: s≤t iff weight(s)=weight(t) and every zero-padded prefix sum of s is at most the corresponding prefix sum of t.

api.name: CharPMZV.dominance.antisymm
api.statement: Mutual prefix dominance implies equality.

api.name: CharPMZV.dominance.depth_antitone
api.statement: s≤t implies depth(s)≥depth(t).

api.name: CharPMZV.dominance.prefix_bound
api.statement: Each prefix sum comparison can be recovered from s≤t.

uses.how: Controls all reduction supports.

items.name: Prefix collapse and coordinatewise tuple sum
items.statement: T_i(s) replaces its first min(i,depth(s)) entries by their sum, leaving the tail, for i≥1 and s nonempty. s+t adds zero-padded coordinates and drops trailing zeros; this differs from concatenation.

api.name: CharPMZV.tuple_operations.collapse_weight
api.statement: T_i preserves weight.

api.name: CharPMZV.tuple_operations.sum_weight
api.statement: weight(s+t)=weight(s)+weight(t).

api.name: CharPMZV.tuple_operations.collapse_monotone
api.statement: T_i(s)≤T_i(t) implies T_k(s)≤T_k(t) for k≥i.

uses.how: Records the correct support order after a prefix is fixed.

items.name: Degree-restricted multiple power sums
items.statement: For nonempty positive s, S_d(s) sums ∏a_i^(−s_i) over monic polynomials with d=deg a_1>⋯>deg a_r≥0; it is zero for d<0. S_<d(s)=Σ_{0≤j<d}S_j(s), and S_<d(empty)=1. No S_d(empty) is needed.

api.name: CharPMZV.degree_sums.cutoff_step
api.statement: For nonempty s, S_<d+1(s)=S_<d(s)+S_d(s), including d<0.

api.name: CharPMZV.degree_sums.depth_zero
api.statement: S_d(s)=0 if d<depth(s)−1.

uses.how: Finite-sum realization of formal relations.

items.name: Thakur multiple zeta value
items.statement: For positive s, ζ_A(s)=Σ_{d≥0}S_d(s) in K∞, equivalently the strictly decreasing-degree monic sum. Set ζ_A(empty)=1.

api.name: CharPMZV.zeta.has_sum
api.statement: The degree sequence is summable and has sum ζ_A(s).

api.name: CharPMZV.zeta.cutoff_limit
api.statement: S_<d(s) tends to ζ_A(s) as d→∞.

api.name: CharPMZV.zeta.frobenius
api.statement: ζ_A(p s_1,…,p s_r)=ζ_A(s)^p.

uses.how: Specialization target of every reduction and independence argument.

items.name: Convergence for every positive index
items.statement: The sum defining ζ_A(s) converges for every positive index: |S_d(s)|≤q^(−d s_1), since tail reciprocal products have norm≤1 and ultrametric finite-sum bounds have no cardinality factor.

items.name: Strict increase of reciprocal power-sum valuations
items.statement: For any positive k and prime power q, S_d(k)≠0 and −deg S_d(k) strictly increases with d≥0. The q=p shortcut is insufficient for general q.
items.locator: Thakur 2009 FFA, §4.1 and proof of Theorem 4 in §5.2
items.note: The external Sheats carry-free greedy-maximum theorem and the positive-exponent passage remain gap G3.

items.name: Nonvanishing of every Thakur MZV
items.statement: For any positive tuple s and any prime power q, ζ_A(s)≠0.

items.name: Thakur, small-entry and q-indivisible index families
items.statement: At weight w>0, I^T_w has all entries≤q and last entry<q; I^0_w has every entry<q; I'_w has no entry divisible by q. Their MZV families are indexed by these finite sets, not silently identified with injective images.

api.name: CharPMZV.index_families.small_sub_thakur
api.statement: I^0_w⊆I^T_w, and equality holds for w≤q.

api.name: CharPMZV.index_families.prime_blocks
api.statement: Replace a=mq+b with 1≤b<q by m copies of q followed by b to map I'_w into I^T_w.

api.name: CharPMZV.index_families.finite
api.statement: Each family is finite as a subset of positive compositions of w.

uses.how: Separates three different families and prevents an all-weight independence claim for I'.

items.name: Weight-w multizeta vector space
items.statement: Z_w is the K-linear span in K∞ of ζ_A(s) for all positive indices of weight w, with Z_0=K·1 as an auxiliary convention.

api.name: CharPMZV.weight_space.mem
api.statement: Each weight-w MZV belongs to Z_w.

api.name: CharPMZV.weight_space.span_universal
api.statement: A K-subspace contains Z_w iff it contains all its indexed generators.

api.name: CharPMZV.weight_space.finite_dimensional
api.statement: There are finitely many compositions of fixed weight, so Z_w is finite dimensional.

uses.how: Dimension and basis statements.

api.name: CharPMZV.dimension_sequence.recurrence
api.statement: At w>q the q-step recurrence holds.

api.name: CharPMZV.dimension_sequence.index_count
api.statement: d(w)=|I^T_w|=|I'_w| for w>0 (proved in counting item).

uses.how: Combinatorial upper bound and dimension equality.

items.name: Counting and block bijection
items.statement: For every w>0, |I^T_w|=|I'_w|=d(w). The block replacement in index-families is a weight-preserving bijection: parse a Thakur word uniquely into runs of q's ending in an entry below q.
items.locator: §1 count; Lemma 6.1; explicit bijection derived here

items.name: Chen correction coefficient
items.statement: For a,b>0 define Δ_i(a,b) in F_p to be (−1)^(a−1) binom(i−1,a−1)+(−1)^(b−1) binom(i−1,b−1) when 0<i<a+b and (q−1)|i, and zero otherwise.

api.name: CharPMZV.chen_coefficient.symm
api.statement: Δ_i(a,b)=Δ_i(b,a).

api.name: CharPMZV.chen_coefficient.support
api.statement: Nonzero coefficients require 0<i<a+b and (q−1)|i.

api.name: CharPMZV.chen_coefficient.small_sum
api.statement: All Δ_i vanish if a+b≤q.

uses.how: Uniform coefficients independent of the degree cutoff.

items.name: Chen's equal-degree product identity
items.statement: For a,b>0 and every integer d, S_d(a)S_d(b)=S_d(a+b)+Σ_{0<i<a+b}Δ_i(a,b)S_d(a+b−i,i).
items.note: G2 is discharged for the actual F_q[θ] consumer by the direct all-exponent/all-degree derivation above. The original Chen article and any additional results in it are not claimed read or extracted.

items.name: Degree-one shuffle relation transfers to every degree
items.statement: An F_p-coefficient identity S_1(a)S_1(b)−S_1(a+b)=Σc_iS_1(a_i,a+b−a_i), with 0<a_i<a+b, for F_q[θ] transfers to every d≥0 (and to any function-field A with a degree-one infinite place).
items.note: The present consumer uses only A=F_q[θ]; the general statement needs the supplier's sign-function interface.

items.name: Controlled fixed-degree product expansion
items.statement: For nonempty indices a,b there exists a finite F_p-linear expansion of S_d(a)S_d(b) into S_d(c), independent of d, with c≤a+b and depth(c)≤depth(a)+depth(b).
items.note: Use simultaneous well-founded recursion with truncated-product, not a circular prerequisite edge; the latter is its second output. No uniqueness of expansions is asserted. The original Thakur 2010 higher-depth proof has a known correction (E9); the simultaneous recursion follows the corrected argument, not its invalid concatenation equality.

items.name: Controlled truncated product expansion
items.statement: For indices a,b, S_<d(a)S_<d(b) is a finite F_p-linear combination of S_<d(c), uniformly in d, with c≤a+b and depth(c)≤depth(a)+depth(b); the empty index acts as the identity.
items.note: The original Thakur 2010 higher-depth proof has a known correction (E9); the simultaneous recursion follows the corrected argument, not its invalid concatenation equality.

items.name: Controlled fixed/truncated product expansion
items.statement: S_d(a)S_<d(b)=S_d(a_1) times the truncated product of a's tail and b, hence admits a finite expansion S_d(a_1,c) with weight preserved and depth at most depth(a)+depth(b).
items.note: The original Thakur 2010 higher-depth proof has a known correction (E9); the simultaneous recursion follows the corrected argument, not its invalid concatenation equality.

items.name: Weight-graded and depth-filtered product formula
items.statement: The product ζ_A(a)ζ_A(b) is an F_p-linear combination of weight weight(a)+weight(b) MZVs of depth≤depth(a)+depth(b).
items.note: The original Thakur 2010 higher-depth proof has a known correction (E9); the simultaneous recursion follows the corrected argument, not its invalid concatenation equality.

items.name: Binary relations as finite coefficient data
items.statement: A weight-w binary relation is two finitely supported K-coefficient families α,β on nonempty weight-w indices such that for every integer d, Σ_s α_s S_d(s)+Σ_t β_t S_{d+1}(t)=0. It is fixed when β=0.

api.name: CharPMZV.binary_relation.zero_add_smul
api.statement: These data form a K-vector space; equality is coefficientwise.

api.name: CharPMZV.binary_relation.evaluate
api.statement: Evaluation at each d gives the certified zero.

api.name: CharPMZV.binary_relation.fixed
api.statement: A fixed relation is exactly an element with zero second coefficient family.

uses.how: Retains relation witnesses rather than assuming independence of realized power sums.

items.name: Summing a binary relation gives an MZV relation
items.statement: For a binary relation (α,β), Σα_sζ_A(s)+Σβ_tζ_A(t)=0; the shift d↦d+1 contributes no boundary term when summed over all integers.

items.name: Carlitz denominator products
items.statement: [i]=θ^(q^i)−θ, D_0=1, D_i=∏_{j=1}^i[j]^(q^(i−j)); also ℓ_0=1 and ℓ_d=∏_{j=1}^d(θ−θ^(q^j)). All nonempty factors are nonzero.

api.name: CharPMZV.carlitz_products.D_recurrence
api.statement: D_i=[i]D_{i−1}^q for i>0.

api.name: CharPMZV.carlitz_products.nonzero
api.statement: D_i and ℓ_i are nonzero in A.

uses.how: Fixes signs and Frobenius powers.

items.name: Carlitz small-exponent power-sum formula
items.statement: For d≥0 and 1≤a≤q, S_d(a)=ℓ_d^(−a). Also for d≥1, S_<d(q−1)=[d]/([1]ℓ_{d−1}^{q−1}).
items.note: Two formulas share the same generating-function calculation. Its general Carlitz interpolation input remains G4.

items.name: Fundamental binary relation R₁
items.statement: For every integer d, S_d(q)+D_1S_{d+1}(1,q−1)=0, hence (1 on (q), D_1 on (1,q−1)) defines R₁∈BR_q.

items.name: Todd's B* operation
items.statement: For v>0 and R=(α,β), multiply S_d(v) by Σ_{j<d}R(j). After expanding products, B*_v(R) is the fixed relation Σα_s S_d(v,s)+Σβ_t S_d(v,t)+Σβ_t S_d(v)S_d(t)=0. Define B*_W by composition in the order w_1,…,w_r, with B*_empty=id.

api.name: CharPMZV.B_operation.fixed_output
api.statement: A nonempty B*_W has zero shifted component.

api.name: CharPMZV.B_operation.weight
api.statement: B*_W increases weight by weight(W).

api.name: CharPMZV.B_operation.fixed_prepend
api.statement: On a fixed relation B*_v simply prepends v to each index.

uses.how: Builds fixed relations with controlled prefixes.

items.name: Small-head simplification of B*
items.statement: If v+t_1≤q for every t in β's support, the last product in B*_v(R) is S_d(v+t_1,t_tail). If β=0, B*_v merely prepends v.

items.name: Todd's C operation
items.statement: For index W, multiply R(d) by S_<d+1(W); split S_<d+1(W)=S_<d(W)+S_d(W) when W is nonempty, and expand fixed, mixed and truncated products into a binary relation C_W(R). Define C_empty=id. Output coefficients are in K, not necessarily F_p.

api.name: CharPMZV.C_operation.weight
api.statement: C_W raises weight by weight(W).

api.name: CharPMZV.C_operation.realization
api.statement: Its evaluated relation is exactly S_<d+1(W)R(d).

api.name: CharPMZV.C_operation.linear
api.statement: For a fixed recursive choice of product expansions, C_W is K-linear on coefficient data.

uses.how: Introduces a bad head q+w_1 with smaller-head remainder.

items.name: Controlled leading term of C_W(R₁)
items.statement: For nonempty W, C_W(R₁) has leading term S_d(q+w_1,W_tail), other S_d(s) with s≤(q)+W and s_1<q+w_1, and shifted terms S_{d+1}(1,t) with t≤(q−1)+W.

items.name: Cancellation operator BC_q
items.statement: For R=(α,β), set BC_q(R)=B*_q(R)−Σ_t β_t C_t(R₁). Its realization is Σα_s S_d(q,s)−D_1Σβ_t S_{d+1}(1)S_<d+1(q−1)S_<d+1(t)=0.

api.name: CharPMZV.BC_operation.cancel
api.statement: The S_d(q,t) and equal-degree product terms cancel exactly.

api.name: CharPMZV.BC_operation.weight
api.statement: BC_q maps BR_w to BR_{w+q}.

api.name: CharPMZV.BC_operation.shifted_support
api.statement: Its shifted terms have first entry 1 and tails dominated by (q−1)+t.

uses.how: Moves each intervening q across a binary relation.

items.name: q-bounded initial prefix and k-admissibility
items.statement: Init(s) is the longest initial subword whose entries≤q, ordered by ordinary finite-list lexicographic order with a proper prefix smaller. s is k-admissible iff its first k zero-padded entries≤q and it is not a word of length≤k with all preceding entries≤q and final entry q.

api.name: CharPMZV.initial_prefix.first_bad
api.statement: If Init(s) is proper then the following entry exceeds q.

api.name: CharPMZV.initial_prefix.full_admissible
api.statement: For k≥weight(s), k-admissibility is equivalent to s∈I^T_weight(s).

api.name: CharPMZV.initial_prefix.monotone_k
api.statement: (k+1)-admissible implies k-admissible.

uses.how: Defines the termination state and detects the terminal-q obstruction.

items.name: Reduction of a first entry exceeding q
items.statement: Suppose s_i≤q for i<k and s_k>q. Then ζ_A(s) is a finite K-linear combination of same-weight ζ_A(t), with depth(t)≥depth(s) and T_k(t)≤T_k(s), of three types: Init increases or stays equal while the k-th entry decreases; all prefix sums from k through depth(s) strictly decrease; or Init strictly increases.
items.note: The three named output classes may overlap. Source issue E3 repairs the unhandled j=0 notation.

items.name: Reduction of a terminal q
items.statement: If every entry of s is≤q and its final entry equals q, then ζ_A(s) is a K-linear combination of same-weight indices with depth≥depth(s), in the decreasing-prefix-sum or increasing-Init classes of Proposition 2.12.

items.name: Finite well-founded reduction rank
items.statement: At fixed positive weight w and fixed k, the reduction branches in Proposition 3.2 terminate. Order first by the induction parameter k and the relevant prefix sum; within a fixed sum use reverse rank of Init in the finite set of weight≤w positive prefixes, then the bad entry. Every branch decreases a component while earlier components stay fixed.
items.locator: Proof of Proposition 3.2, pp.14–15; formalization of its stabilization argument
items.note: A bounded lexicographic order on arbitrary variable-length words would not by itself prove termination. This item is the finite fixed-weight argument, not an asserted unrestricted lex well-order.

items.name: k-admissible reduction theorem
items.statement: For every positive index s and k≥1, ζ_A(s) is a finite K-linear combination of ζ_A(t) for k-admissible t with weight(t)=weight(s), depth(t)≥depth(s), and T_k(t)≤T_k(s).

items.name: All-weight Thakur spanning theorem
items.statement: For every w>0, the family {ζ_A(s):s∈I^T_w} spans Z_w over K.

items.name: All-weight dimension upper bound
items.statement: For every w>0, dim_K Z_w≤d(w). This does not assert all-weight linear independence.

items.name: Precise boundary of Todd's relation-generation conjecture
items.statement: The assertion that the relations B*_U C_V(R₁), with weight(U)+weight(V)=w, span every K-linear relation in weight w+q (w>0) is a conjecture here, not a theorem or prerequisite of Theorems A–D.

api.name: CharPMZV.ToddConjecture.statement
api.statement: The conjecture compares the span of the displayed formal relation family with the kernel of MZV realization.

uses.how: Records context without promoting conjectural completeness to a proved result.

items.name: Completed algebraic closure and Carlitz period setting
items.statement: Choose the standard embedding of K into the completion C∞ of an algebraic closure of K∞, with |θ|=q. C∞ is complete, algebraically closed and perfect of characteristic p; choose a compatible Carlitz period π̃.
items.note: DM.2 explicitly uses the completed algebraic closure; its reviewed audit does not find this normed characteristic-p object in the pinned baseline.

api.name: CharPMZV.C_infinity.embedding
api.statement: The K∞ embedding into C∞ is isometric.

api.name: CharPMZV.C_infinity.frobenius_equiv
api.statement: The q-power map is an automorphism of C∞.

api.name: CharPMZV.C_infinity.period_choice
api.statement: Changing the selected Carlitz period multiplies it by F_q^×.

uses.how: Analytic coefficient field.

items.name: Restricted power-series carrier
items.statement: For a normed ultrametric ring R, PowerSeries.IsRestricted 1 f means its coefficient norms tend to zero; PowerSeries.IsRestricted.subring 1 packages these series as a subring. This supplies a carrier conditional on the C∞ norm, not the full Tate Banach/entire-function theory.

api.name: CharPMZV.restricted_carrier.coeff_limit
api.statement: At radius 1 the restricted condition is exactly coefficient norm→0.

api.name: CharPMZV.restricted_carrier.subring_coe
api.statement: The restricted subring inherits addition and multiplication from formal power series.

api.name: CharPMZV.restricted_carrier.polynomial
api.statement: A polynomial is restricted because all sufficiently high coefficients vanish.

uses.how: Reuses the exact existing carrier rather than rebuilding it.

items.name: Coefficient Frobenius twists
items.statement: For n∈Z and f=Σa_i t^i over C∞, f^(n)=Σa_i^(q^n)t^i, using iterated inverse Frobenius for n<0. Extend coefficientwise to rational functions, restricted/entire series and matrices wherever defined.

api.name: CharPMZV.twist.ring_equiv
api.statement: Each twist is a ring automorphism and preserves polynomial t-degree.

api.name: CharPMZV.twist.coefficient
api.statement: coeff_i(f^(n))=(coeff_i f)^(q^n).

uses.how: Difference equations and pole-orbit arguments.

items.name: Skew-polynomial carrier
items.statement: Given a ring R equipped with the required multiplicative-N action, SkewPolynomial R is its skew monoid algebra; monomial multiplication is X^n(r)·X^m(s)=X^(n+m)(r φ^[n](s)). The action instance is part of the input.

api.name: CharPMZV.ore_carrier.monomial_mul
api.statement: The coefficient is r times φ iterated n on s.

api.name: CharPMZV.ore_carrier.scalar
api.statement: Degree-zero monomials embed R.

api.name: CharPMZV.ore_carrier.action_required
api.statement: Instantiating inverse-q twist requires an explicit compatible action.

uses.how: Existing generic carrier; not a pre-existing Carlitz/Ore Frobenius instance.

items.name: Effective dual t-motives
items.statement: Use barK[t,σ] with σ f=f^(−1)σ. An effective dual t-motive is a left module finite free over barK[t], whose σ-cokernel is killed by a power of t−θ; morphisms commute with this action. Finite freeness over barK[σ] is not part of this definition.
items.note: Route to DM.4 as a missing refinement, not an exact match to its contravariant Anderson-motive equivalence with additional finite-generation hypotheses.

api.name: CharPMZV.dual_motive.basis_matrix
api.statement: For a chosen column basis m, σm=Φm defines a polynomial matrix Φ.

api.name: CharPMZV.dual_motive.hom_intertwining
api.statement: A linear map is a motive map iff its matrix satisfies the chosen-basis semilinear intertwining equation.

api.name: CharPMZV.dual_motive.trivial
api.statement: The trivial rank-one motive has σ acting by coefficient twist and Φ=1.

uses.how: Fixes the dual convention and the exact effective range.

items.name: Rigid analytic trivialization
items.statement: For a polynomial difference matrix Φ, a rigid analytic trivialization is Ψ∈GL_r(T) satisfying Ψ^(−1)=ΦΨ, where T is the radius-one Tate algebra over C∞.

api.name: CharPMZV.rigid_trivialization.equation
api.statement: Entrywise coefficient twist of Ψ equals ΦΨ.

api.name: CharPMZV.rigid_trivialization.basis_change
api.statement: For a basis change U, transform Φ and Ψ consistently with semilinearity.

api.name: CharPMZV.rigid_trivialization.invertible
api.statement: Invertibility is over T, not merely over its fraction field.

uses.how: Connects explicit period matrices to generic DM.8 machinery.

items.name: ABP ring of algebraic entire functions
items.statement: E consists of f=Σa_i t^i with a_i∈barK, lim |a_i|^(1/i)=0, and [K∞(a_0,a_1,…):K∞]<∞. This is a coefficient-field finiteness condition in addition to convergence on every disc.

api.name: CharPMZV.entire_ring.evaluate
api.statement: Every f∈E can be evaluated at any point of C∞.

api.name: CharPMZV.entire_ring.ring
api.statement: E is closed under addition, multiplication and coefficient twists.

api.name: CharPMZV.entire_ring.include_tate
api.statement: E embeds into the radius-one Tate algebra.

uses.how: Correct input domain of the lifting theorem.

items.name: Carlitz factorials
items.statement: For n≥1 with n−1=Σn_jq^j in base q, Γ_n=∏D_j^{n_j}; for a tuple s put Γ_s=∏Γ_{s_i}.

api.name: CharPMZV.gamma.digits
api.statement: The factorial uses the q-adic digits of n−1.

api.name: CharPMZV.gamma.nonzero
api.statement: Γ_n and Γ_s are nonzero in A.

api.name: CharPMZV.gamma.tuple_append
api.statement: Γ_{s++t}=Γ_sΓ_t.

uses.how: Prevents the factorial index shift.

items.name: Anderson–Thakur polynomials in the manuscript indexing
items.statement: Put γ_0(t)=1 and γ_j(t)=∏_{ℓ=1}^j(θ^(q^j)−t^(q^ℓ)). Define α_n(t) by Σ_{n≥1}(α_n(t)/Γ_n)x^n=x/(1−Σ_{j≥0}(γ_j(t)/D_j)x^(q^j)); H_n is α_n with θ and t interchanged.

api.name: CharPMZV.AT_polynomials.coefficient
api.statement: The generating function uniquely determines α_n coefficientwise.

api.name: CharPMZV.AT_polynomials.swap
api.statement: The involution exchanging θ and t takes α_n to H_n and back.

api.name: CharPMZV.AT_polynomials.external_index
api.statement: This H_n equals H_{n−1} in Chang 2014 §5.5.

uses.how: Provides interpolation and the low-weight difference equation.

items.name: Anderson–Thakur growth bound
items.statement: For every n≥1, the Gauss norm satisfies ||H_n||<|θ|^{nq/(q−1)}.
items.locator: §4.2; Chang 2014 Theorem 5.5.1 with the index shift
items.note: The interpolation source theorem and its proof dependencies remain G4.

items.name: Low-weight Anderson–Thakur formula
items.statement: H_n=1 for 1≤n≤q. For 1<k≤q−1, H_{q+k−1}=(t^q−t)+(k−1)(t^q−θ^q), with the integer coefficient reduced in characteristic p.

items.name: Anderson–Thakur Ω function
items.statement: With a compatible choice of (q−1)-st root of −θ, Ω(t)=(-θ)^{−q/(q−1)}∏_{i≥1}(1−t/θ^(q^i)). It is an entire Tate unit, satisfies Ω^(−1)=(t−θ)Ω, and Ω(θ)=π̃^(−1).
items.note: Construction and zero/period identities require the generic analytic inputs recorded as G5; do not infer them from the restricted carrier alone.

api.name: CharPMZV.omega.zeros
api.statement: Ω has simple zeros at θ^(q^j) for j≥1, all outside the unit disc.

uses.how: Provides the weight-filtering zeros and period normalization.

items.name: Entire multiple Ω–H series
items.statement: For positive s=(s_1,…,s_r), define L(s)=Σ_{i_1>⋯>i_r≥0}(Ω^{s_r}H_{s_r})^(i_r)⋯(Ω^{s_1}H_{s_1})^(i_1), and L(empty)=1.

api.name: CharPMZV.L_series.tail_recursion
api.statement: Separate i_r=0 from i_r>0 to obtain the Frobenius recursion.

api.name: CharPMZV.L_series.weight
api.statement: Each summand has total Ω weight weight(s), with twists retained.

api.name: CharPMZV.L_series.empty
api.statement: L(empty)=1 and has no summation indices.

uses.how: Period functions specialized in every independence argument.

items.name: Entire convergence of L(s)
items.statement: For every positive s, the series L(s) belongs to E.
items.note: The analytic-growth proof is decomposed in entire-from-equation; Lang's isogeny and the complete Tate norm interface remain G5.

items.name: Anderson–Thakur interpolation of power sums
items.statement: For s≥1,d≥0, (H_sΩ^s)^(d)(θ)=Γ_s S_d(s)/π̃^s, using the manuscript's H_s indexing.
items.note: Original Anderson–Thakur 1990 proof not yet read; exact exported statement is fixed in G4.

items.name: Specialization of L(s) at θ
items.statement: L(s)(θ)=Γ_s ζ_A(s)/π̃^{weight(s)}.

items.name: Specialization at the Frobenius orbit
items.statement: For each positive integer N, L(s)(θ^(q^N))=L(s)(θ)^(q^N).

items.name: Difference matrix for an index
items.statement: For s of depth r, index rows/columns by i=0,…,r. Put u_i=Σ_{j=i+1}^r s_j. Set Φ_{ii}=(t−θ)^{u_i}, Φ_{i,i−1}=H_{s_i}^(−1)(t−θ)^{u_{i−1}} for 1≤i≤r, and other entries zero.

api.name: CharPMZV.single_motive_matrix.diagonal
api.statement: The final diagonal entry is 1 and determinant is (t−θ)^{Σ_i u_i}.

api.name: CharPMZV.single_motive_matrix.subdiagonal
api.statement: Only the immediately lower diagonal can be nonzero off the diagonal.

api.name: CharPMZV.single_motive_matrix.prefix_submatrix
api.statement: The upper-left r×r block is Φ'_s.

uses.how: Polynomial system for the L-series.

items.name: Period matrix for an index
items.statement: Using the preceding u_i, set Ψ_{ij}=0 for i<j and Ψ_{ij}=Ω^{u_i}L(s_{j+1},…,s_i) for i≥j. Thus the diagonal is Ω^{u_i}, and the last row lists L of suffixes and 1.

api.name: CharPMZV.single_period_matrix.diagonal
api.statement: Ψ_{ii}=Ω^{u_i}.

api.name: CharPMZV.single_period_matrix.invertible
api.statement: The determinant is a power of the Tate unit Ω.

uses.how: A concretely indexed trivialization suitable for reuse.

items.name: The single-index period equation
items.statement: Ψ_s^(−1)=Φ_sΨ_s, with Ψ_s invertible over T and all its entries in E; the same equation holds for their upper-left blocks.

items.name: ABP analytic-to-entire criterion
items.statement: If Φ∈Mat_l(barK[t]), det Φ(0)≠0, ψ∈T^l and ψ^(−1)=Φψ, then every coordinate of ψ lies in E.
items.note: Lang and the complete nonarchimedean analytic interface remain G5.

items.name: Conjugate size over a perfect closure
items.statement: For a finite separable extension L_0/K, put L=∪L_0^{q^(−ν)}, O the integral closure of A in L, O_0=O∩L_0. Define ||x|| as the maximum of |τx| over K-conjugates, and coefficient/matrix size as the maximum of entry sizes.
items.locator: ABP 2004 §§3.2–3.3.1, with its k=our K and its K=our L

api.name: CharPMZV.ABP_size.submultiplicative
api.statement: Size is submultiplicative and ultrametric.

uses.how: Arithmetic estimates used in the lifting proof.

items.name: Positive-characteristic Liouville bound
items.statement: If f(z)=Σa_i z^i∈O[z] is nonzero and λ≠0 is a root of multiplicity ν, then |λ|^ν≥(max_i||a_i||)^{−[L_0:K]}.

items.name: Riemann–Roch lattice count for ABP
items.note: The high-degree Riemann–Roch theorem is verified at the pinned Tau Ceti commit. G6 now concerns the exact-constant-field, infinity-divisor and all-conjugate-norm bridge, not finding or re-planning Riemann–Roch.

items.name: Thue–Siegel kernel bound
items.statement: For C>1, 0<r<s and M∈Mat_{r×s}(O) with ||M||<C, there is nonzero x∈O^s such that Mx=0 and ||x||<C^{r/(s−r)}.

items.name: Polynomial-matrix Thue–Siegel bound
items.statement: For C>1, 0<r<s and M∈Mat_{r×s}(O[t]) with ||M||<C, there is nonzero x∈O[t]^s with Mx=0 and ||x||<C^{r/(s−r)}.

items.name: ABP auxiliary polynomial row
items.statement: In the normalized integral setting of ABP §3.4.2 with l>1 and N a sufficiently large positive multiple of 2l, there is nonzero h∈O[t]^{1×l} of uniformly bounded conjugate size and deg_t h<(1−1/(2l))N, such that E=hψ vanishes at θ^{q^{−(N+ν)}} for 0≤ν<N.
items.note: The precise uniform constant and the normalization inequalities are not yet turned into signatures; retain G7 rather than presenting this source-subsetting as a closed proof leaf.

items.name: Vanishing of the ABP auxiliary entire function
items.statement: Under the same normalized hypotheses, for sufficiently large N the auxiliary entire function E=hψ constructed in §3.4.3 is identically zero.

items.name: Anderson–Brownawell–Papanikolas lifting criterion
items.statement: Let Φ∈Mat_l(barK[t]) have det Φ=c(t−θ)^m with c∈barK^× and m≥0. If ψ∈E^l satisfies ψ^(−1)=Φψ and ρ∈barK^{1×l} satisfies ρψ(θ)=0, there is P∈barK[t]^{1×l} with Pψ=0 and P(θ)=ρ.
items.locator: Theorem 4.2, corrected nonzero c; ABP 2004 Theorem 3.1.1 and §3.4
items.note: All actual matrices used in the main manuscript have nonzero determinant. E4 concerns the broader printed theorem, not the validity of these applications.

items.name: Frobenius-invariant common denominator
items.statement: For Φ_i∈Mat_{r_i}(barK[t]) with det Φ_i=c_i(t−θ)^{m_i}, c_i≠0, and F∈Mat_{r_1×r_2}(barK(t)) satisfying F^(−1)Φ_2=Φ_1F, the monic least common denominator of the entries of F belongs to F_q[t].
items.note: Use the rational coefficient domain corrected in E10; the full proposition proof was read and the printed page visually checked.

items.name: Frobenius fixed fields and Tate intersection
items.statement: The inverse-coefficient-twist fixed field of barK(t) is F_q(t). Its intersection with the radius-one Tate algebra is F_q[t].
items.note: The denominator may have a zero root; nonzero finite-field-algebraic roots have norm one. Do not assume every root has norm one.

items.name: Chang's MZ property
items.statement: A nonzero Z∈barK∞ has weight-w MZ property if a polynomial system ψ^(−1)=Φψ of rank d≥2 satisfies the ABP determinant hypothesis, has last column (0,…,0,1)^T, has ψ∈E^d with first entry at θ equal to π̃^(−w) and last cZπ̃^(−w) for c∈K^×, and at θ^(q^N), N>0, only the final entry can survive, equal to (cZπ̃^(−w))^{q^N}.
items.note: barK∞ here denotes the algebraic closure of K∞ inside C∞, as in Chang's setting; the actual MZVs lie in K∞.

api.name: CharPMZV.MZ_property.witness
api.statement: Export the matrix/vector, coefficient c and all specialization identities.

api.name: CharPMZV.MZ_property.tensor
api.statement: Tensoring witnesses gives the MZ property of products, with weights added.

api.name: CharPMZV.MZ_property.MZV_witness
api.statement: The single-index period matrix supplies a witness for every nonzero MZV.

uses.how: Correct descent theorem input.

items.name: Separating highest-weight relations
items.statement: For finitely many MZ-property values of finitely many positive weights, an algebraic linear relation involving a maximal-weight block forces an algebraic relation among the maximal-weight values alone.

items.name: Descent of same-weight independence
items.statement: Let V be a finite set of nonzero MZ-property values of the same positive weight. K-linear independence of V implies barK-linear independence.
items.locator: Chang 2014 Theorem 3.4.5, §4.2 Step II; main §5 (wrong proposition locator E5)

items.name: MZVs satisfy Chang's MZ property
items.statement: For every nonempty positive index s, ζ_A(s) has the MZ property of weight weight(s), with nonzero normalization Γ_s.

items.name: Merged proper-prefix index set
items.statement: For distinct nonempty indices s_i of the same weight w, I is the union of all proper prefixes, including empty. Each t∈I has weight<w; a nonempty t has unique parent obtained by deleting its last entry. Order I by length, then lexicographically, for triangular matrices.

api.name: CharPMZV.prefix_index.dedup
api.statement: Shared prefixes give one row/column, not separate copies.

api.name: CharPMZV.prefix_index.parent
api.statement: The parent of every nonempty member is again in I.

api.name: CharPMZV.prefix_index.terminal_unique
api.statement: At fixed total weight w, a proper prefix t can be the penultimate prefix of at most one s_i.

uses.how: Deduplication essential to the independence induction.

items.name: Prefix difference matrix and extension row
items.statement: For t∈I put u_t=w−weight(t). Let Φ'_{t,t}=(t−θ)^{u_t}, and for a nonempty prefix t=(v,a), Φ'_{t,v}=H_a^(−1)(t−θ)^{u_v}; other entries are zero. For a relation with nonzero a_i∈A, transfer a_i(θ) to a_i(t)∈F_q[t]. Put v_t=a_i(t)H_last(s_i)^(−1)(t−θ)^{u_t} when t is its penultimate prefix, and zero otherwise. Let Φ=[[Φ',0],[v,1]].

api.name: CharPMZV.prefix_Phi.well_defined
api.statement: Terminal uniqueness makes v_t unambiguous.

api.name: CharPMZV.prefix_Phi.determinant
api.statement: det Φ=∏_{t∈I}(t−θ)^{u_t}, with nonzero leading coefficient 1.

api.name: CharPMZV.prefix_Phi.last_column
api.statement: The last column of Φ is the last standard basis vector.

uses.how: Exact polynomial matrix of the combined extension.

items.name: Prefix period matrix and linear-relation row
items.statement: For prefixes u,v∈I, put Ψ'_{u,v}=L(u after v)Ω^{w−weight(u)} if v is a prefix of u, and zero otherwise. Put f_t=Σ_{i:t proper prefix of s_i}a_i(t)L(s_i after t). Define Ψ=[[Ψ',0],[f,1]].

api.name: CharPMZV.prefix_Psi.empty_component
api.statement: f_empty=Σ_i a_i(t)L(s_i).

api.name: CharPMZV.prefix_Psi.diagonal
api.statement: Ψ'_{t,t}=Ω^{w−weight(t)}.

api.name: CharPMZV.prefix_Psi.suffix_row
api.statement: Every f_t is an explicitly indexed finite sum of suffix L-functions.

uses.how: Encodes every lower-weight suffix relation simultaneously.

items.name: Merged-prefix rigid trivialization
items.statement: Ψ^(−1)=ΦΨ; Ψ is invertible over T and all entries lie in E. If Σ_i a_i(θ)Γ_{s_i}ζ_A(s_i)=0, then f_empty(θ)=0.

items.name: Normalized ABP row for a putative MZV relation
items.statement: Under the preceding relation, ABP produces a polynomial row (g_t,g) annihilating the first column ψ of Ψ, with g_t(θ)=0 and g(θ)=1. Dividing by g gives a rational row G=(g_t/g,1), regular at θ, with Gψ=0.

items.name: Eliminating the difference of a normalized lift
items.statement: Assume all relevant lower-weight suffix MZVs are K-independent, hence barK-independent. Then B=G−G^(−1)Φ is zero.

items.name: Polynomial splitting row over a common F_q denominator
items.statement: There is nonzero monic b∈F_q[t] such that δ_t=b g_t/g∈barK[t], and the row δ satisfies δ=δ^(−1)Φ'+bv. Equivalently the lower-unitriangular gauge splits the combined extension.

items.name: Rationality of suffix period combinations
items.statement: For every proper prefix t, f_t(θ) belongs to K.

items.name: Carlitz-period power field criterion
items.statement: For an integer n>0, π̃^n∈K∞ iff (q−1)|n. In particular a nonzero Eulerian normalized MZV in K forces its weight divisible by q−1.
items.note: The exact compatible period/product comparison is part of G5.

items.name: Eulerian isolated tails
items.statement: If a proper prefix t belongs to exactly one s_i in a putative relation, then ζ_A(s_i after t)/π̃^{w−weight(t)}∈K, and its positive suffix weight is divisible by q−1.

items.name: Longest-common-prefix contradiction for small entries
items.statement: Suppose all s_i have entries in {1,…,q−1}, are distinct of the same weight and occur with nonzero coefficients in a relation. Past the last shared prefix of any branch, isolated-tail divisibility forces every remaining entry after the branch to equal q−1. Choosing two indices with maximal common prefix makes their first differing entries congruent modulo q−1, hence equal, a contradiction.

items.name: All-weight independence of small-entry MZVs
items.statement: For every w>0, the family indexed by I^0_w is K-linearly independent (and therefore barK-linearly independent).

items.name: Thakur basis through weight q
items.statement: For 1≤w≤q, I^T_w=I^0_w, and the corresponding MZVs form a K-basis of Z_w with dimension d(w).

items.name: Eulerian suffix-weight constraint for q-indivisible indices
items.statement: In the induction proving Theorem 6.2, assume all smaller-weight I' families are independent. For any nonempty proper prefix t in a putative weight-w I' relation, q−1 divides w−weight(t). Consequently every entry after the first in each participating index is divisible by q−1.

items.name: Only two possible indices in the remaining small-weight relation
items.statement: For q>2 and q<w≤2q−2, the preceding constraints force every index in a putative I'_w relation to be (w) or (k,q−1), where k=w−(q−1) and 2≤k≤q−1. Thus the only possible nontrivial relation is a_1Γ_wζ_A(w)+a_2ζ_A(k,q−1)=0 with a_1,a_2∈K^×.

items.name: Two-row polynomial splitting system
items.statement: For w=q+k−1, 2≤k≤q−1, the relation yields nonzero a_1(t),a_2(t)∈F_q[t] and δ_1,δ_2∈barK[t] with δ_1=(δ_1^(−1)+δ_2^(−1)H_k^(−1)+a_1(t)H_w^(−1))(t−θ)^w and δ_2=(δ_2^(−1)+a_2(t)H_{q−1}^(−1))(t−θ)^{q−1}. Common denominator b is absorbed into the a_i.

api.name: CharPMZV.small_weight_system.scale
api.statement: Multiplying δ_1,δ_2,a_1,a_2 by any f∈F_q[t] preserves the equations.

api.name: CharPMZV.small_weight_system.second_row
api.statement: The second row uses H_{q−1}=1.

api.name: CharPMZV.small_weight_system.nonzero_coefficients
api.statement: The a_i remain nonzero after clearing the common denominator.

uses.how: Input to the explicit integral-descent and degree-bound argument; its scope matches the instance attributed to Kuan–Lin by the manuscript.

items.name: Integral descent and theta-degree bound for the two-row system
items.statement: For the small-weight system with q>2, w=q+k−1 and 2≤k≤q−1, every polynomial solution δ_1,δ_2∈barK[t] already lies in A[t]=F_q[θ,t]. Moreover δ_2=0 or deg_θ δ_2≤q, and δ_1=0 or deg_θ δ_1≤floor(qw/(q−1)). No extra scaling is needed.
items.locator: §6 p.23, citing Kuan–Lin 2016 proof of Theorem 2
items.note: G1 is discharged for this exact instance by the explicit independent derivation, not by claiming access to Kuan–Lin Theorem 2. The manuscript’s citation is preserved in the locator; the original external theorem remains unread. The manuscript quotes Kuan–Lin for δ_1, δ_2 ∈ K[t], while its coefficient comparison needs A[t]; this item supplies the latter (E11).

items.name: Solving the second small-weight equation
items.statement: Every solution δ_2∈barK[t], a_2∈F_q[t] of (6.4), with H_(q−1)=1, has a_2=f(t)(t^q−t) and δ_2=f(t)(θ^q−t^q) for a unique f∈F_q[t]. If a_2≠0 then f≠0.
items.note: This classification works directly over barK[t] and does not need the degree bound; the dependency edge to degree-descent is removed.

items.name: Interior-weight coefficient contradiction
items.statement: Using integral descent, if 2≤k<q−1 the degree bound forces δ_1=(aθ+b)(t−θ)^w with a,b∈F_q[t]. Substitution in the twisted first equation forces a=b=0, then f=(k−1)a_1 and (t^q−t)a_1=0, contradicting a_1≠0.
items.note: The polynomial forms now follow from degree-descent and integral-monic-quotient, including when p divides k−1.

items.name: Endpoint-weight coefficient contradiction
items.statement: Using integral descent, at k=q−1 and w=2q−2 write δ_1=(aθ²+bθ+c)(t−θ)^w. Coefficients θ^{2q−1} and θ^{2q−2} give aθ²+bθ+c=a(t−θ)². Put h=a(t^q−t)−a_1. The resulting identity h[(t−θ^q)²−(t−θ)^{2q}]=(θ^q−t^q)f(t^q−t) is impossible when f≠0.
items.note: The explicit θ=t step includes the h=0 case suppressed by the manuscript's final divisibility sentence.

items.name: q-indivisible independence through weight 2q−2
items.statement: For q>2 and 1≤w≤2q−2, the MZV family indexed by I'_w is K-linearly independent.
items.note: Statement faithfully extracted. The base case should read w ≤ q (E12), and the coefficient comparison needs δ_i ∈ A[t] (E11, supplied by degree-descent).

items.name: Thakur basis through weight 2q−2
items.statement: For every prime power q and 1≤w≤2q−2, the MZVs indexed by I^T_w form a K-basis of Z_w, and dim_K Z_w=d(w).
items.note: No claim here that the 2021 paper proves the later all-weight basis theorem.

items.name: Failure of the q-indivisible independence method at 2q−1
items.statement: For q>2, ζ_A(2q−1) and ζ_A(1,2q−2) are K-linearly dependent; both indices belong to I'_{2q−1}. This prevents extending Theorem 6.2's exact family to the next weight.
items.note: This is not a disproof of the Thakur family basis conjecture: the two index families are different.

items.name: Explicit next-weight binary relation
items.statement: For every prime power q and integer d, S_d(2q−1)+D_1 S_{d+1}(1,2q−2)=0; consequently ζ_A(2q−1)+D_1ζ_A(1,2q−2)=0.
items.locator: Remark 6.3, explicitly derived by expanding C_(q−1)(R₁)

items.name: Support control after BC_q cancellation
items.statement: After expanding the shifted products in BC_q(R), every resulting shifted index is (1,u) where u≤(q−1)+t for some t in the old shifted support; the fixed part consists of (q,s) for s in the old fixed support.

items.name: Dimension lower bound from small entries
items.statement: For w>0, dim_K Z_w is at least the number of positive compositions of w with each part<q. With c(0)=1 and c(n)=0 for n<0, this count satisfies c(w)=Σ_{i=1}^{q−1}c(w−i).

items.name: Finite-field power sum over units
items.statement: For a finite field F of cardinality q and i∈N, Σ_{c∈F^×} c^i is −1 when q−1 divides i and 0 otherwise. Reindexing by inversion gives the identical formula for c^(−i).
items.note: The library statement is for natural positive powers; inverse powers use the bijection c↦c⁻¹. It includes i=0, where q−1=−1 inside F.

items.name: Explicit two-pole binomial decomposition
items.statement: In any field, for nonzero x,y with h=x−y≠0 and integers a,b>0, (x^a y^b)⁻¹ = Σ_{j=1}^a (−1)^b binom(a+b−j−1,b−1)/(x^j h^(a+b−j)) + Σ_{j=1}^b (−1)^(b−j) binom(a+b−j−1,a−1)/(y^j h^(a+b−j)). Integer coefficients map to the field.
items.locator: Worker derivation supplying §2.1 equation (2.1), expanded in the report
items.note: This is an explicit coefficient application, not a replacement for Mathlib’s general partial-fraction existence/uniqueness theory. Chen 2015 itself remains unread; this proof does not claim to transcribe Chen’s proof.

items.name: Reindexing distinct equal-degree monic pairs
items.statement: For d≥0, ordered distinct monic degree-d pairs (u,v) are in bijection with (u,h) where u is monic of degree d and 0≠h∈F_q[θ] has degree<d, by h=u−v; also with (v,h) by u=v+h. Every such h has a unique form c g with c∈F_q^× and g monic of degree<d. Thus for i>0, Σ_{0≠h,deg h<d} h^(−i)=−1_{q−1|i} S_<d(i).

items.name: Polynomial descent for a monic difference equation
items.statement: Let E be a characteristic-p field, q=p^e with e>0, and R⊆E a subring stable under q-power. Twist coefficients while fixing t. If B,F∈R[t], B is monic of degree m>0, and δ∈E[t] satisfies δ^(1)=Bδ+F, then δ∈R[t].

items.name: Theta-degree bound for a scalar Frobenius equation
items.statement: Let q=p^e≥2, A=F_q[θ], m>0, M≥0, G∈A[t] with deg_θ G≤M (G=0 allowed), and δ∈A[t] satisfy δ^(1)=(t−θ^q)^m(δ+G). Then δ=0 or deg_θ δ≤max(M, floor(qm/(q−1))).
items.locator: Worker derivation for the required §6 degree bound

items.name: Integral quotient by the t-minus-theta factor
items.statement: For δ∈A[t], A=F_q[θ], if (t−θ)^m divides δ in barK[t], then δ=(t−θ)^m R with R∈A[t]. For δ≠0, deg_θ R=deg_θ δ−m after identifying A[t] with F_q[t][θ].
items.locator: Worker derivation for the coefficient comparisons on §6 p.24

items.name: Existing high-degree function-field Riemann–Roch
items.statement: For fields k,F with a k-algebra structure, IsFunctionField k F and IsIntegrallyClosedIn k F (the exact constant-field condition), if D is a divisor with deg D≥2 genus(k,F)−1, then dim_k L(D)=deg D+1−genus(k,F), as an equality of integers.
items.note: The exact constant-field hypothesis is essential. This is the existing theorem to import, not a new roadmap target; transporting ABP’s all-conjugate norm bound to such a divisor remains G6.

items.name: Products of small power sums
items.statement: For positive integers a, b with a + b ≤ q and every integer d, S_d(a)S_d(b) = S_d(a+b).
items.locator: Remark 2.2(2), p. 8; used in the proof of Corollary 2.7, p. 9
items.note: Added by cc-442dc5; the paper states it as an elementary fact. Without it Corollary 2.7 has no source item.

items.name: Uniqueness of rigid analytic trivializations up to F_q(t)
items.statement: Let Φ ∈ Mat_r(K̄[t]) with det Φ = c(t−θ)^s, c ∈ K̄^×, and let Ψ ∈ GL_r(T) satisfy Ψ^(−1) = ΦΨ. If X is a matrix with entries in the fraction field of T satisfying X^(−1) = ΦX, then X = Ψν for a matrix ν with entries in F_q(t).
items.note: Added by cc-442dc5. It turns (5.6) into (5.7). DM.8 plans the rigid analytically trivial motives of Papanikolas' theory, of which this is a basic lemma; twist-fixed records only the fixed field of K̄(t).
